dedupe_keys.name: waste wise cities tool wact un habitat method for sdg 11 6 1 municipal solid waste data

description: The Waste Wise Cities Tool is UN-Habitat's step-by-step method for collecting data on how much municipal solid waste a city generates, how much is collected, and how much ends up in facilities with adequate environmental control, which is SDG indicator 11.6.1. UN-Habitat developed it under its Waste Wise Cities programme and has applied it with partners in many cities in Africa, Asia and Latin America. The tool guides users through seven steps with a household survey guide for waste generation, a questionnaire to trace the recovery chain of materials, and criteria to rate the control level of waste facilities. It is free to download from UN-Habitat's website and is intended for any city. Caveats: results depend on survey sample sizes and local teams, facility control ratings involve judgement, and the tool measures the waste system at one point in time, not simulating it. Simulation uses: preparing input data on generation, collection coverage and facility capacity for waste system models, setting a baseline for capacity planning and climate adaptation of waste services, and comparing cities. Related records: the World Bank What a Waste database (data-what-a-waste-global-database) holds country and city waste statistics, and SWEET (model-sweet-solid-waste-emissions-estimation-tool) turns similar data into emission estimates.
name: Waste Wise Cities Tool (WaCT): UN-Habitat method for SDG 11.6.1 municipal solid waste data

sources.note: WaCT guides readers through 7 steps to collect data on MSW generated, collected and managed in controlled facilities; household survey guide, questionnaire on the MSW recovery chain and criteria for environmental control level of facilities

title_en: Waste Wise Cities Tool (WaCT): UN-Habitat method for SDG 11.6.1 municipal solid waste data
